discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 051741
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1241 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Patchy drizzle and showers at times. Not as warm with highs 
  only in the 50s. 

- Lake effect rain tonight through Friday, tapering off 
  Saturday morning. 

- Seasonably cold this weekend with highs in the 50s. Cold
  Sunday morning with lows near freezing.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 203 AM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

A 996mb low swirls over the UP this morning (bringing much needed 
rain to a drought-striken area), with a secondary shortwave trough 
aloft digging into extreme eastern Iowa. This has spawned a fairly 
widespread area of rain and drizzle upstream. This feature is 
still digging south-southeast this hour but is expected to lift 
northeast this afternoon. As it does so, scattered showers will 
move through for the afternoon. Remaining somewhat breezy once 
more with a modest pressure gradient still in play. Temperatures
only in the 50s today with only modest cold air advection noted
aloft due to boundary- parallel flow. However, a strong push of
CAA rushes in this evening/tonight as the primary trough axis 
(digging in through Minnesota this morning) sweeps through. This
CAA and lift promotes widespread showers followed by lake 
effect rain showers. If you're a snow lover, this is truly a 
waste of what would otherwise be an impressive lake effect snow 
set up. High resolution CAMS suggest QPF through the event 
of 0.30-0.50". Equilibrium levels crest at nearly 9,000 ft, 
indicative of excellent lake induced lift. A single band of 
rain is anticipated late Thursday night through Friday night 
that follows the eastern shore and wavers over La Porte and 
western St. Joseph (IN) counties. Lake effect comes to and end 
Saturday morning as equilibrium levels fall in response to 
rising heights aloft with the parent trough moving off. 

Compared to recent temperatures, very cold early Sunday morning in 
the wake of this system as skies clear and high pressure descends 
over the Great Lakes. Lows will be near freezing which is just shy 
of normal: 35 degrees. Over the course of next week, a classic sine 
wave pattern takes shape at 500mb with a towering Central US
ridge bookended by troughs. We'll be on the edge of seasonably 
cool northwest flow. If northwest flow wins out, we could see 
episodes of light rain (though Pacific moisture transport is 
poor). Alternatively, mild and dry conditions could prevail if 
the ridge to our west shifts east late in the week.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 1239 PM EST Thu Nov 5 2026

A complicated interaction between three areas of vorticity controls 
our weather at the local level for this taf period. MVFR CIGs will 
still be possible this afternoon as our main upper low slowly 
meanders northeastward and dampens out. Those CIGs will be more 
probable at SBN than FWA, but will become even more probable overall 
as a cold front pushes through the area. This is in conjunction with 
a vigorous shortwave sliding southeastward down Lk MI. That doesn't 
really get to the tear drop of the lake until around 12z tonight and 
there's not a whole lot of lake induced instability with only around 
15 to 20C Delta T. So would expect a multicellular disorganized area 
of lake effect rain to get under way Friday. A combination of 
trajectories and wind convergence appear to take the best area of 
precipitation south of FWA, but mostly through SBN with a quick time 
period potentially west of SBN. This would lead to a continuation of 
MVFR CIGs and times of MVFR VISBY, especially as the main cold front 
swings through.  Overall, trajectories will be veering from 
southwesterly to northwesterly through the period. Additionally, 
focused on either side of FROPA, sustained winds above 10 kts will 
be likely.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 7 PM EST Friday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown
AVIATION...Roller

spc.text:
SPC AC 051610

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1010 AM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 051630Z - 061200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely today and tonight.

   ...Mid Atlantic to southern New England...
   Broad southwesterly flow aloft is present today over the eastern
   states, with a moist surface air mass in place along and east of the
   Appalachians.  Forcing will be weak through the day, but an
   approaching upper trough over the central US will result in
   increasing thunderstorm potential after dark - especially from the
   Mid Atlantic region northward into southern New England.  Strong
   winds aloft will result in fast-moving storms, but nocturnal cooling
   will limit surface-based convective threat and the overall risk of
   damaging winds.  Nevertheless, an occasional storm could pose some
   concern for gusty winds.

   ...KS/OK...
   A mid-level shortwave trough and associated pocket of cold mid-level
   air will result in steep lapse rates and scattered afternoon
   thunderstorms over parts of southern KS and northern OK.

   ..Hart/Supinie.. 11/05/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.summary: A few strong to severe storms are possible Friday over parts of the eastern Carolinas and southeast Virginia.
spc.text:
SPC AC 051653

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1053 AM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 061200Z - 071200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS POTIONS
   OF THE EASTERN CAROLINAS AND SOUTHEAST VIRGINIA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few strong to severe storms are possible Friday over parts of the
   eastern Carolinas and southeast Virginia.

   ...Eastern Carolinas and southeast Virginia...

   A belt of enhanced deep-layer southwesterly flow will be in place
   across much of the Eastern Seaboard on Friday as an upper trough
   pivots east toward the Atlantic coast. A surface front extending
   from southern New England south/southwest to central GA Friday
   morning will likewise shift eastward through the period. Ahead of
   the front, mid 60s F dewpoints will be in place as far north as
   southeast VA. 

   Within the warm advection regime ahead of the front, showers and
   thunderstorms will be ongoing across portions of the region. Coupled
   with associated cloud cover, daytime heating will be limited,
   suppressing stronger destabilization despite cooling aloft. Midlevel
   flow increasing to around 30-40 kt will support effective shear
   magnitudes around 35-45 kt as convection along the front moves into
   the moist downstream airmass across the eastern Carolinas and
   southeast Virginia. This may support organized cells/bows capable of
   producing damaging gusts and perhaps a brief tornado. However, the
   severe risk should remain fairly isolated given expected poor
   low-level lapse rates and modest instability.

   ..Leitman.. 11/05/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 050814

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0214 AM CST Thu Nov 05 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are unlikely on Saturday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move across the northeastern states on Saturday
   with another shortwave aloft diving southeastward across the upper
   MS Valley. This will support cool conditions as high pressure
   settles into the MS/OH Valleys, with offshore winds across the Gulf
   and Atlantic coasts. High pressure will also exist across the Great
   Basin, behind an upper low dropping southeastward into Mexico. As
   such, little if any instability will be present to support
   thunderstorms over land.

   ..Jewell.. 11/05/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
